messages:
maria-cs: FYI, Crescent is getting mixed 429 and 401 errors during our SDK boot in their staging. Ticket #C-421. They said it started after they flipped their edge gateway yesterday.
liam-eng: Can you paste a minimal failing request? Are these coming from many distinct clients or a single host?
maria-cs: Single host for now. Here's the payload they sent (sanitized):
```
POST /v1/generate
Authorization: Bearer <jwt>
Content-Type: application/json
{
  "model": "redwood-1",
  "input": "hi"
}
```
They see a 401 once every ~10 requests, and 429s in bursts (~30s windows).
zara-ps: Two quick suspects: 1) gateway is mutating headers (we've seen it trim long Authorization on some nginx configs), 2) client clock skew causing our JWT checks to reject intermittently. Do they use a short TTL token?
maria-cs: Their token TTL is 15s (refreshing frequently). They use a serverless pool that pre-warms a bunch of lambdas.
sam-sre: Short TTL + bursty concurrency = stampede of refreshes. Also if the gateway rewrites Authorization sometimes the signature fails -> 401. Can you ask them to add request-id and a small debug header so we can correlate?
liam-eng: If they can reproduce, ask them to run this quick probe and paste headers/responses: 
```bash
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H "X-Debug-Id: probe123" https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -d '{"model":"redwood-1","input":"probe"}'
```
That will show if headers arrive intact.
maria-cs: Sent instructions. Also told them to capture a sequence of 10 requests. Will paste logs.
deploy-bot: deploy made by liam-eng at 2026-03-21T09:12:00Z :rocket:
liam-eng: If gateway is nginx, check `proxy_set_header Authorization $http_authorization;` sometimes missing in custom snippets. Without that we see Authorization stripped intermittently when proxy chains are present.
zara-ps: Another mitigation: increase token TTL to 60s while we diagnose (less frequent refresh storms). And add jitter to refresh to avoid synchronized bursts.
maria-cs: They just replied: logs below (they redacted tokens):
```
[2026-03-21T09:20:13Z] 200 OK X-Debug-Id=probe123 req=abc123
[2026-03-21T09:20:13Z] 401 Unauthorized X-Debug-Id=probe124 req=abc124 auth=missing
[2026-03-21T09:20:14Z] 429 Too Many Requests X-Debug-Id=probe125 req=abc125 rate=client_concurrency
[2026-03-21T09:20:15Z] 200 OK X-Debug-Id=probe126 req=abc126
```
They see Authorization sometimes flagged as missing.
sam-sre: That aligns with header being dropped mid-chain. Could be a limit on header size too if their auth header includes long cookies. Any reverse proxies in front? (Cloud CDN, WAF?)
maria-cs: Yep, they have a WAF and an API gateway for routing. They said after they bumped the WAF rules it started.
liam-eng: Ask them to bypass the WAF for a minute (or add a rule to forward Authorization untouched) and retry. If 401s disappear, it's the WAF.
zara-ps: Also recommend they switch to short-lived signed cookies for session outside of Authorization header if the WAF mangles headers, but that's more of a product change for them.
maria-cs: They've temporarily disabled a couple WAF rule groups. Retesting now.
maria-cs: Update: 10 test requests -> 10x 200. No 401s, very few 429s (still some bursts). They say reducing concurrent refreshes helped.
liam-eng: Great. Next steps: 1) keep WAF rule that caused header rewrite disabled or adjust to forward, 2) raise TTL to 60s + add jitter on refresh, 3) keep eye on 429 windows and if persistent, we can whitelist their IP at the edge for onboarding.
zara-ps: I'll draft a short onboarding checklist for them: how to configure common gateways (nginx, envoy), token TTL guidance, and client refresh jitter. Can share as a gist.
maria-cs: Perfect. I'll update the ticket with mitigations and ask for a post-mortem of their WAF rule change. Thanks all :thumbsup:
liam-eng: If they want, we can provision a temporary elevated rate window for 24h to smooth the onboarding ramp.
maria-cs: I'll offer that as an option. Closing loop with customer now.
